author: k946838651
quote:
The biggest issue with this GTAVI is that it lacks the cynical, rebellious edges, which are the simmering discontent from those on the margins that defined earlier GTA titles.

It feels more like empty, self-indulgent posturing.

Take GTA IV for instance, its opening sequence, set against the backdrop of a dark night on a cargo ship, managed to lay out and interweave everything: 

The diamonds, the smuggled immigrants, the Eastern European mob, and a stifling, xenophobic New York(Liberty City).

In contrast, this game rambles on and on without ever getting to the point.

Lucia and Jason just act like robots, going through the motions without ever offering a personal perspective or opinion of their own.

Everything they do feels like a forced, reactive response to external pressures rather than a choice driven by who they are.

This episode completely fails to deliver the kind of focused characterization and nuanced portrayal of the protagonist seen in the fourth and fifth entries. 

Instead, all I see is a hollow, stereotypical collection of abstract descriptors. The creators clearly haven’t spent any time on the ground or engaged with real people.

Overall, I see only a domesticated form of rebellion with huge influencial of DEI and Feminist.
